findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

Black specks were observed on ice in the ice machine. The PIC was shown and removed the ice to correct the immediate violation. The machine is also observed soiled, refer to line item #49 for the write up. Ensure that all ready to eat foods are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzles of both soda guns are observed soiled. One was observed with a yellow slimy substance on the surface of the spouts. The other has a brown lumpy substance coming out of one of the spouts. Both items were shown to the PIC and were cleaned during this inspection to correct. Employees stated that the guns are stored in soda water nightly. The inspection indicated that this may help with cleaning frequency, but the nozzles still need regular cleaning (wash/rinse/sanitize) to be maintained in a clean and safe state.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The ice machine has a small amount of mold growth developing on the deflector shield. The bartender was shown and cleaned the location during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

During this inspection the PIC was unable to provide documentation verifying that employees are aware of their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis. While looking through folders blank copies of the Reporting Agreements given out by this department were found. The PIC is instructed to make copies and have all employees sign a copy prior to the follow up in ten days.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The hand sink in the bathroom closest to the stage appears to have run out of soap. The PIC was notified and replaced the soap during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks maintain a supply of hand soap at all times.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The ice machine has a small amount of mold growth developing around the moist outer edge where the lid opens and closes. The bartender was shown and cleaned the location during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The mop sink in the facility is observed clogged during this inspection and the sink is holding standing water. The situation was noted with the PIC and they are instructed to repair prior to the follow up. The inspector is unable to conducted a follow up on the normal three day follow up and will conduct it on day four (Friday).

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Only one of the employees currently employed at this facility and without a Certified Food Protection Manager certification has a current food handler certification available at the facility. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to ensure that all employees acquire an ANSI accredited Food Handler certification prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Both soda guns in the bar area are soiled. The nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) often enough to be maintained clean and safe for service.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

On arrival test strips effective for CL based sanitizers were available. The facility is currently using a Quat based sanitizer. The situation was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the tests trips available for use match the sanitizer used in the facility. Test strips were acquired during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

The only employee at the facility during this inspection does not have a certified food protection manager certification (CFPM). Per him, they prepare foods while here alone. Due to being a Class-II facility, a CFPM must be available at the facility at all times that foods are served/handled. Hand outs were available and they were instructed to ensure that a CFPM is always available in the future. The managers arrived during the inspection and indicated that the employees are signed up to take an upcoming class.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without paper towels during this inspection. When asked about hand drying at the sink the PIC indicated an empty paper towel dispenser. Ensure that paper towels are supplied at the hand sinks at all times. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The bar three part sink showed less than 100 ppm quat on inspector test strips. A minimum of 200 ppm is required per the instructions on the bottle. PIC indicated that the sink was made when they arrived around noon. The sink was remade during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The deflector shield is observed soiled during this inspection. It was cleaned with a sani rag during this inspection to correct. 2) Both soda guns in the bar area are HEAVILY soiled. PIC indicated that they should be soaked and cleaned every day, but this appears to be several days (possibly weeks) of accumulation observed. The nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during this inspection to correct the violation.
